Key by hand. kT = 86.1733 ueV/K x 0.1100 K = 9.4791 ueV; eps/kT = 0.60133; f = 1/(1 + e^0.60133) = 0.35404. Spin-degenerate level at zero field: in-rate 2 Gamma f, out-rate Gamma (1 - f). Record length T = N (1/Gamma_in + 1/Gamma_out), so 1/Gamma = 2 T f (1 - f) / (N (1 + f)) = 2 x 1000 x 0.35404 x 0.64596 / (355 x 1.35404) = 0.95154 ms. Far above the reservoir the electron escapes at Gamma: mean time 0.95 ms. Check: occupied fraction 2f/(1 + f) = 0.523, as in the record.

Most tempting wrong answer: leaving out the spin factor (in-rate Gamma f) gives 1/Gamma = T f (1 - f)/N = 0.64 ms. A count that misses short visits (about 285) gives 1.19 ms.

Check program (Python 3, standard library):
import math
f = 1 / (1 + math.exp(5.70 / (86.173333e-3 * 110.0)))
tau = lambda n: 2 * 1000.0 * f * (1 - f) / (n * (1 + f))
print(f"f = {f:.5f}")
print(" ".join(f"{n}:{tau(n):.4f}" for n in range(350, 361)))
